Stambaugh et al. research factors

Source: R/data.r
stambaugh.Rd

Return (factors) and level (risk free rate) time series for various research asset pricing factors put together by Robert F. Stambaugh and collaborators including Lubos Pastor and Yu Yuan. The factors include liquidity (traded & non-traded), market, size as well as two 'mispricing' factors: management & performance. All factors are constructed from US stocks; see Details for the verification against the source papers.

data(stambaugh)

Format

A data.table with variables:

  • frequency: factor return frequency (day, month); character.

  • factor: Stambaugh factor; character. One of non-traded liquidity, traded liquidity, size, management, performance, market, risk free rate.

  • period: period over which factor returns are calculated or risk free rate level is observed; character, YYYYMM for monthly and YYYYMMDD for daily observations.

  • value: corresponding return (factors) or level (risk free rate) observation; numeric.

Source

https://fnce.wharton.upenn.edu/profile/stambaug/ (the former finance.wharton.upenn.edu/~stambaug/ address redirects there); the data files are served from faculty.wharton.upenn.edu. Liquidity factors: Pastor & Stambaugh (2003), "Liquidity Risk and Expected Stock Returns", Journal of Political Economy 111(3), 642-685, doi:10.1086/374184 . Size, management, performance, market and risk free rate: Stambaugh & Yuan (2017), "Mispricing Factors", The Review of Financial Studies 30(4), 1270-1315, doi:10.1093/rfs/hhw107 .

Details

Region: US, verified against both papers. Their factor universes are ordinary common shares listed on NYSE/AMEX/NASDAQ (CRSP data), so every row is US. The dataset itself has no region column; all_factors adds region = "US" to every Stambaugh row.

Coverage: liquidity 196208-202512 (traded liquidity from 196801; earlier observations are missing in the source file); mispricing factors monthly 196301-201612 and daily 19630102-20161230. The author has not refreshed the mispricing files past 2016.

market is the excess market return plus the risk free rate (MKTRF + RF); risk free rate is RF.

Rebuild with data-raw/rebuild_stambaugh.R (cached downloads; the build functions are tested against saved fixtures).
